`native.tsv` is generated by `tools/generate_consensus_fixtures.py` against
mmx-node `ca6438b37c08007106d58efe4a990f6ecb276649`. Ordinary Rust tests do not
require native libraries, a running node, a wallet or chain data.

Each row contains tab-separated fields:

1. Case name.
2. Parameter profile (0: native defaults with network `mainnet`; 1: small custom
   fee constants; 2: fee constants set to `UINT64_MAX`).
3. Original self-describing VNX bytes in hex.
4. Native static validity (`0`, `1` or `ERR` for an exception).
5. Native static cost (or `ERR`).
6. Contract `num_bytes()` (or `ERR`, or `-` for other types).
7. Hash with `hash_version=0`, `full_hash=false`.
8. Hash with `hash_version=0`, `full_hash=true`.
9. Hash with `hash_version=1`, `full_hash=false`.
10. Hash with `hash_version=1`, `full_hash=true`.
11. Transaction ID preimage in hex (`-` for other types).
12. Transaction content-hash preimage in hex (`-` for other types).

Transactions always select their own version, and solution/result hashes always
use version 0. `ERR` preserves the native exception boundary; message text is
not compared. Cost profiles 1 and 2 deliberately do not reseal transaction
static costs, allowing validation ordering and overflow behavior to be checked.

`authorization.tsv` is generated by `tools/reference_authorization.cpp` through
the same generator (`--suite authorization`). It compares native
`Contract::validate` directly and the signature-selection/lookup portions of
`Node::validate` / `Node::execute`. It does not claim full Node validation.

Its columns are case, mode (`contract`, `sender`, `input`, `user`), transaction
version, transaction ID, VNX contract/transaction bytes, VNX solution/lookup record
bytes (`-` for none), input/operation index, initial read cost, gas limit, final
read cost, ordered lookup addresses (`-` for none), result class (`ok`, `static`,
`dynamic`) and native error text (`-` on success). Injected lookups charge 1017
units (1000 base plus an authoritative index cost of 17) before returning a
record or absence, and preserve the native cost precheck.

Replay the crypto fixture first to seed the same signature-cache history. Tests
reconstruct native diagnostic text from typed authorization errors to compare
failure reasons, owner addresses and ordering as well as the failure class.
